label: self-hosting for beginners
meta_title: What Is Self-Hosting? A Beginner's Guide
meta_description: Self-hosting means running your own apps on a computer you control. Learn what it is, why people do it, and how to start, no Linux or Docker knowledge needed yet.

label: what I host
meta_title: What Can You Self-Host? Apps People Run
meta_description: Photos, passwords, notes, media, ad blocking and more. See what you can actually self-host, which apps are worth running first, and what's better to skip.

label: the basic setup
meta_title: How Self-Hosting Works: The 5 Core Parts
meta_description: Every self-hosted setup is the same five parts: server, app, storage, network, and access. Understand how they fit together, with a real app as an example.

label: pick a server
meta_title: How to Choose a Home Server for Self-Hosting
meta_description: How to choose a first home server: what actually matters (RAM, storage, power, noise), why an old PC works to start, and when a mini PC or Raspberry Pi is worth buying.

label: pick an OS
meta_title: How to Choose a Home Server OS
meta_description: How to choose an OS for your home server. Why plain Linux (Ubuntu or Debian) plus Docker is the safe pick, with honest notes on CasaOS, TrueNAS, Unraid and Proxmox.

label: install the OS
meta_title: Install a Home Server OS & Find Its IP
meta_description: Flash a USB or use Raspberry Pi Imager, run the installer, enable SSH, connect the server to your network, find its IP, and give it a fixed address.

label: linux + SSH
meta_title: Linux & SSH Basics to Run Your Home Server
meta_description: The little bit of Linux you need to run a server: connect over SSH, move around folders, edit files, and update the system with about ten commands.

label: meet Docker
meta_description: Images, containers and ports explained simply, then install Docker and Compose on your server and run a test container to check everything works.

label: install first app
meta_title: Install Your First Self-Hosted App with Docker
meta_description: A beginner walkthrough: make a folder, write a docker-compose.yml, run docker compose up, and open your first self-hosted app in the browser. No experience needed.

label: Docker Compose
meta_description: Reading a docker-compose.yml for self-hosting: what image, ports, volumes, environment and restart mean, plus the commands to start, stop, log, and update apps.

label: storage & volumes
meta_description: Where your self-hosted app data actually lives. Docker named volumes vs bind mounts, and how to keep your files safe when you update or rebuild a container.

label: best first apps
meta_description: The best self-hosted apps for beginners to try first: Homepage, Memos, Linkwarden, FreshRSS and Uptime Kuma. Low-risk, useful, and easy to install with Docker.

label: backups
meta_title: How to Back Up Self-Hosted Apps
meta_description: What to back up, how to automate it, the 3-2-1 rule, and why to test a restore before you trust your server with photos, passwords, or anything you can't lose.

label: access at home
meta_description: Why server-ip:port is fine to start, using a dashboard as your front door, and the optional step up to real names and HTTPS with a reverse proxy.

label: remote access
meta_title: Access a Home Server Remotely with Tailscale
meta_description: Reach your self-hosted apps from anywhere without exposing them. How Tailscale works, with honest takes on Cloudflare Tunnel, WireGuard and port forwarding.

label: full walkthrough
meta_description: The whole path in one checklist: server, OS, SSH, Docker, your first app, storage, backups, and remote access, every step tied together from a bare machine.
